results.title: RBI MPC Meeting October 2026 Highlights: RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra announces 25 bps repo rate hike; your EMIs set to go up - The Times of India
results.content: “Three main reasons why the Monetary Policy Committee decided to hike the policy rate by 25 basis points to 5.5% and change the policy stance from neutral to calibrated tightening in its October 2026 monetary policy review relate to its assessment that (1) inflation in India has become more generalized and persistent, (2) supply side risks remain high due to global crude and commodity price uncertainties and adverse impact of strong El Niño conditions and (3) a relatively high growth momentum [...] RBI MPC Meeting October 2026 Live Updates: The Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) has been tasked with keeping the retail or Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation within the 2-6% range with 4% as the ideal target. In recent months due to the persistent US-Iran war, crude oil prices have risen, leading to imported inflation and a rising retail inflation number. While still within RBI’s range, the deficit monsoon is also adding inflationary pressures. [...] RBI’s 2026-27 growth projections at 7.1% highlights a lowering of the growth momentum in subsequent quarters after the record 7.8% growth in 1Q 2026-27. In spite of the October rate hike, RBI sees CPI inflation going up to 6.0% in 3Q and 5.7% in 4Q 2026-27. These are the upper limits of the MPC’s tolerance range and one more hike in the policy rate in the December 2026 policy meeting may not be ruled out.

results.title: The repo rate is 5.50% from 7 October 2026, up from 5.25%
results.content:
The hike reverses part of the 125 basis points of cuts made in 2025, which took the repo rate from 6.50% to 5.25%. The rate then stayed at 5.25% for four meetings in 2026.

The RBI announced no change to the cash reserve ratio (CRR), the share of deposits that banks must keep with the RBI. It stands at 3.00%. [...] | Measure | Before (August 2026) | After (7 October 2026) |
 --- 
| Policy repo rate | 5.25% | 5.50% |
| Standing deposit facility (SDF) rate | 5.00% | 5.25% |
| Marginal standing facility (MSF) rate and Bank Rate | 5.50% | 5.75% |
| Policy stance | Neutral | Calibrated tightening |
| CPI inflation forecast, 2026-27 | 5.0% | 5.2% |
| Real GDP growth forecast, 2026-27 | 6.7% | 7.1% | [...] Four things will shape the December decision:

 Inflation data. The CPI figures for September and October 2026 will show whether inflation is tracking the RBI’s 6.0% forecast for the December quarter.
 Crude oil. Prices rose sharply in September, which the Governor linked to the West Asia conflict.
 The rupee. A weaker rupee would add to the cost of imports.
 Rabi sowing. A weak winter crop would keep food prices high.
